correction: STORY-01-007 wired the otel-collector service in docker-compose.yml with a bind-mount to _infra/docker/observability/otel-config.yaml, but never wrote the config file itself. On first `compose up`, Docker silently created an empty DIRECTORY at the bind-mount path, and the collector crashed with `read /etc/otel/config.yaml: is a directory`.
pattern: Whenever a generated docker-compose service declares a bind-mount to a host file (volumes: ./path/to/file.ext:/container/path), that host file MUST be authored in the same skill run. Bind-mounts to non-existent host paths cause Docker to auto-create an empty directory, which then masquerades as a 'file' to the container and produces confusing 'is a directory' errors. Before finishing, the skill must enumerate every `volumes:` entry whose source is a file path (has an extension) and assert the source file exists on disk with non-empty content.

correction: STORY-01-010's reconciliation integration test was emitted at tests/utils/test_reconciliation_integration.py. It boots a real SparkSession (via pyspark.importorskip + delta), so a stale Py4J/PySpark venv produces _start_update_server() arity errors that turn the unit-test job red even though no unit code is broken. Worse, STORY-01-002 AC5 runs bare `pytest tests/utils/` which picks up this integration test by path and fails-closed. The unit/integration split has to be enforced by layout, not just by marker.
pattern: Integration tests (any test that imports pyspark, boots a SparkSession, requires Docker, or talks to UC OSS / Marquez) MUST be emitted under tests/integration/<layer>/, NEVER under tests/<layer>/ alongside unit tests. The marker @pytest.mark.integration is required but not sufficient — the path itself encodes the contract so that `pytest tests/<layer>/` is unambiguously unit-only. Additionally: when the scaffold writes a Makefile, `make test` MUST be `uv run pytest -m "not integration" tests/` (or equivalently `uv run pytest tests/<layer>/ tests/<layer>/ ...` excluding tests/integration), and a separate `make integration-test` target MUST run `uv run pytest -m integration tests/integration/`. Story ACs that assert `pytest tests/utils/` green should be regenerated to assert `make test` green so the AC tracks the Make-target contract, not a path that may include integration tests.

correction: STORY-01-007's Dockerfile.airflow used `FROM python:3.12-slim` (rolling tag). When Debian 13/trixie became the default slim base, the build started failing with `apt-get install openjdk-17-jdk-headless` exit 100 because trixie dropped openjdk-17 in favor of openjdk-21. Previous successful builds were either before the tag rolled or relied on a stale local layer cache, masking the regression until a fresh build.
pattern: Always pin Debian releases explicitly in container base images. NEVER use floating tags like `python:3.12-slim`, `debian:slim`, `ubuntu:latest`, or any tag that omits the distro release codename. Use the release-pinned form: `python:3.12-slim-bookworm`, `debian:12-slim`, `ubuntu:24.04`. When the LLD pins a system package (JDK version, Spark version, glibc), the Dockerfile MUST pin the base distro release that ships that package — verify the package exists in the chosen release before emitting the FROM line. This eliminates the entire class of bug where the same Dockerfile builds today, breaks tomorrow when the upstream rolling tag rotates, and the local layer cache hides the regression until a clean rebuild.

correction: STORY-01-007 Dockerfile.airflow fetched Spark from `https://dlcdn.apache.org/spark/spark-4.0.0/spark-4.0.0-bin-hadoop3-scala2.13.tgz`. The URL had two bugs: (a) `dlcdn.apache.org` is a rolling mirror that only serves the CURRENT release line — once Spark 4.0.0 was superseded (by 4.0.2 / 4.1.1) the dlcdn path returned 404; (b) starting with Spark 4.x, Scala 2.13 is the default and the binary name has NO `-scala2.13` suffix — the correct artifact is `spark-4.0.0-bin-hadoop3.tgz`. The mv target path was also wrong for the same reason.
pattern: When fetching pinned versions of Apache project releases (Spark, Kafka, Flink, Hadoop, etc.) in a Dockerfile or installer, NEVER use `https://dlcdn.apache.org/` — that mirror only carries the currently-supported releases, so pins to older versions silently start 404-ing the moment Apache rotates them. ALWAYS use `https://archive.apache.org/dist/` for version-pinned downloads, which preserves every historical release. Additionally, verify the exact artifact name for the target version against the archive directory listing before emitting the URL — naming conventions change across major versions (e.g. Spark 3.x ships `-bin-hadoop3-scala2.13.tgz`, but Spark 4.x drops the `-scala2.13` suffix because Scala 2.13 is the only build). The skill MUST `curl -sI` the resolved URL during generation and fail loudly if it 404s, rather than emitting an untested URL.

correction: The create-scaffold skill emitted a custom `Dockerfile.airflow` (FROM python:3.12-slim, download Spark binary from dlcdn) that diverged from the canonical cookiecutter template (FROM apache/airflow:3.2.1-python3.11, install pyspark via pip with no Spark binary download). The custom file shipped both L-002 and L-003 bugs; the template did not. The divergence was invisible until the build actually ran, because nothing in the skill or downstream validators compares rendered output against the template.
pattern: Always render scaffold files BY APPLYING the cookiecutter template, NEVER by re-deriving them from the LLD inline. Specifically: any file that has a corresponding source under `inputs/lld/v*/templates/cookiecutter-chapter/{{cookiecutter.chapter_name}}/{{cookiecutter.project_name}}/...` MUST be produced by cookiecutter variable substitution on that source — not by the skill authoring a parallel implementation. After every create-scaffold run the skill MUST diff every rendered file against the template source (post variable substitution) and FAIL LOUDLY if any path under the template exists in patient_360/ with materially different content. This catches the silent-divergence class of bug where the LLD describes a service one way, the template encodes a tested way, and the skill emits a third untested way.

correction: patient_360/_infra/docker/docker-compose.yml mapped Marquez API to host port 5000 (`5000:5000`), colliding with macOS AirPlay Receiver which binds 0.0.0.0:5000 by default on macOS 12+. The cookiecutter template (`inputs/.../docker-compose.yml`) already maps host 5001 -> container 5000 specifically to dodge this collision, but the scaffold skill rendered a divergent file with the wrong mapping (same class as L-004). Result: `make dev-up` failed with `bind: address already in use` on a stock macOS dev machine.
pattern: When emitting host-port mappings in a Dockerfile / docker-compose for a project that may be developed on macOS, NEVER bind host ports 5000 or 7000 — Apple's AirPlay Receiver and AirTunes claim those ports by default on macOS 12+ and the user cannot change that without disabling AirPlay system-wide. Pick a non-reserved host port (5001+, 7001+) and document the mapping in a comment. Prefer parameterized form via env-var with a safe default: `"${SERVICE_HOST_PORT:-5001}:5000"` so developers can override without editing the compose file. This rule applies to ANY service whose canonical default port is 5000 or 7000 (Marquez API, Flask default, Python http.server default). Additionally — see L-004 — the rendered compose file MUST match the template; the skill should diff every rendered _infra/docker/* path against `inputs/lld/v*/templates/.../...` and fail loudly on divergence.

correction: patient_360 docker-compose.yml + the cookiecutter template both set the Airflow service healthcheck to `curl http://localhost:8080/health`. Airflow 3.x moved that endpoint to `/api/v2/monitor/health`; the legacy `/health` returns 404. Result: every Airflow container Docker brings up is marked `unhealthy` forever, Airflow itself runs fine, but `docker compose up --wait` blocks until timeout and `make dev-up` exits with code 1. Confirmed in patient_360-airflow: /health => 404, /api/v2/monitor/health => 200.
pattern: When emitting a healthcheck for a vendor service (Airflow, Marquez, Unity Catalog, Postgres, etc.), pin the health URL to the version-specific path documented for the pinned image — and verify it returns 200 against that image BEFORE writing the compose. For Airflow specifically: 1.x/2.x served `/health`, 3.x serves `/api/v2/monitor/health` (the v1 API was removed and `/health` returns 404). Whenever the LLD pins an Airflow major version >=3, the healthcheck MUST use the v2 monitor endpoint. As a general rule, never copy a healthcheck URL from older docs without re-verifying against the pinned image — vendors routinely renumber API paths across majors, and Docker silently keeps the container in `unhealthy` state when the check 404s.

correction: patient_360 + cookiecutter template + LIBRARIES.md all pin `pyspark==4.0.0`. That release is broken: `pyspark/core/context.py:309` calls `_start_update_server(auth_token)` with one arg, but `pyspark/accumulators.py:357` requires `(auth_token, is_unix_domain_sock, socket_path=None)` — a two-arg minimum. Every SparkContext init in PySpark 4.0.0 raises `TypeError: _start_update_server() missing 1 required positional argument: 'is_unix_domain_sock'`. The bug blocks any code that imports pyspark and boots a SparkSession: unit tests, integration tests, and the runtime DAG. Upstream fixed it in 4.0.1 (line 309 now passes is_unix_domain_sock). The same bug was previously misdiagnosed in L-001 as 'Py4J version drift' and worked around by routing integration tests via marker — but the real defect is PySpark 4.0.0 itself.
pattern: NEVER pin `pyspark==4.0.0` — that exact version ships a regression in `pyspark/core/context.py` that breaks every SparkSession boot with a TypeError on `_start_update_server`. Pin `pyspark>=4.0.2,<4.1` (last patch in the 4.0 line, fully wire-compatible with a Spark 4.0.0 JVM) or upgrade to `pyspark==4.1.1` if the LLD's Spark JVM pin permits the 4.1 line. Before emitting any PySpark pin in a Dockerfile, pyproject.toml, or LIBRARIES.md, the skill MUST `pip install <pin>` in a throwaway venv and run `python -c 'from pyspark.sql import SparkSession; SparkSession.builder.master("local[1]").getOrCreate().stop()'` — if SparkContext init raises, the pin is rejected. The earlier 'pyspark/py4j version drift' workaround in L-001 (marker-based unit/integration split) does NOT fix this — it only hides the symptom in unit tests; integration runs, smoke-se, and the Bronze DAG still die. The honest fix is to bump the pin off 4.0.0.

correction: validate-ingestion check_soft_import_removed flags try/except ImportError around se_runner as CRITICAL once se_runner.py ships, but LLD §8.6 + §13 Decision 14 (Resolved 2026-05-11) explicitly require keeping it as a diagnostic-only fail-closed wrapper that re-raises. STORY-01-009 ships this pattern with a passing test.
pattern: When the validator finding contradicts the latest LLD revision, do NOT remove the diagnostic try/except ImportError wrapper from ingestion_runner.py — it is mandated by LLD §8.6 + §13 Decision 14. The validator rule check_soft_import_removed needs to be updated to recognize the diagnostic-only pattern (log + re-raise) as compliant, distinct from the legacy soft-import bootstrap (swallow + continue).
applied_note: Rewrote check_soft_import_removed -> check_se_import_wrapper using AST. Now distinguishes re-raising diagnostic wrapper (OK per §8.6) from swallowing soft-import (CRITICAL when se_runner.py shipped). Back-compat alias retained.

correction: Forked Skill invocations of create-dag/update-ingestion sometimes return without running Phase 0 resolver — `.skill-arg`/`.skill-paths` remain on disk and the skill claims no user request was given. create-ingestion appears more reliable.
pattern: When a forked skill returns asking for a target, the orchestrator should retry with the conversational arg explicitly OR detect that .skill-arg was not consumed (file still present after invocation) and surface a CRITICAL halt rather than silently moving on.

correction: STORY-02-005 AC1/AC3 specify dq_rules/synthea_*.yml but LLD §5.1 + project CLAUDE.md use dq_rules/{table}.yml convention
pattern: When story AC glob conflicts with LLD/project convention, halt and recommend scrum-master:update-stories rather than rename project-wide

correction: contracts/{table}.yml in STORY-02-001 AC is a reference (existing contract used by ingestion runner), not a scaffold deliverable; classifier grouped it under scaffold but the sub-skill correctly ROUTE-OUTed.
pattern: When a path appears under a glob pattern like `contracts/{table}.yml` inside an AC line that describes ingestion behaviour, treat it as a reference dependency, not a scaffold deliverable; DELIVERABLE-OWNERS.yaml should distinguish contracts paths only when the AC explicitly says create/update/author/define.

correction: STORY-02-005 AC2/AC3 verification spec uses equals:13 (row_dq) and equals:6 (action_if_failed) — counts file occurrences not files-with-rule. Real files have multiple rules per YAML per DQS spec; spec should use min:13 / min:6 with per-file constraint.
pattern: When AC Verification uses grep_count equals:N where N == file count, but each file legitimately contains multiple matches, the verification spec is wrong; flag to scrum-master for spec correction rather than reduce real rule content.

correction: STORY-02-001 plan routed contracts/*.yml to update-scaffold but the AC only READS those contracts (existing files); update-scaffold correctly ROUTE-OUT. The deliverable-extractor should not classify backtick-quoted read references as scaffold deliverables.
pattern: When extract-deliverables sees a backtick-quoted path that already exists AND is referenced in an AC as a source/input (e.g. "uses StructType from contracts/{table}.yml"), do not emit a scaffold task. Only emit a task for the skill that owns the AC verb ("adds", "writes", "calls", "creates").

correction: validate-ingestion check_soft_import_removed flags the try/except ImportError block as CRITICAL referencing LLD §8.5, but LLD v1.11 (2026-05-11) §8.6 + §13 Decision 14 Resolved EXPLICITLY require keeping the try/except for diagnostic logging + re-raise. The failclosed unit test (test_ingestion_runner_failclosed_unit.py) also asserts the wrapper is present.
pattern: Validator rule check_soft_import_removed in developer-plugin/skills/validate-ingestion/scripts/validate_ingestion.py is stale vs LLD v1.11 §8.6 / §13 Decision 14 (Resolved 2026-05-11). It must be inverted: the diagnostic try/except wrapping `from {project}.utils import se_runner` is REQUIRED, not forbidden, when se_runner.py is shipped. Remove the CRITICAL flag (or invert to require the wrapper) and update the docstring to cite §8.6 instead of §8.5.
applied_note: Rule rewritten as check_se_import_wrapper. Uses AST to detect whether the ImportError handler re-raises (compliant per §8.6) vs swallows (legacy bootstrap, CRITICAL when SE shipped). Validated with 5 case sanity tests covering all (wrapper-shape × se_runner-presence) combinations.

correction: Handbook validator (validate_ingestion.py) runs project-wide and CRITICALs on sibling-story gaps (e.g. ingestion_factory.py, per-table configs owned by STORY-02-002). Halting STORY-02-001 on these is a false-positive — its own ACs all PASS via verify_acs.py.
pattern: When the handbook validator (Step 3.4) reports CRITICAL issues, intersect each finding against the current task's paths/groups before halting. CRITICALs that name paths owned by sibling stories (not in this task's .skill-paths) should be recorded as out-of-scope and not halt the current story. Halt only when a finding cites a path the current task was responsible for.

correction: Handbook validator (validate_ingestion.py) reports project-wide failures including paths owned by later stories in the same batch; halting the first story on those failures incorrectly cascades.
pattern: When the handbook validator runs after a story dispatch, filter its CRITICAL findings to ones touching the current story task paths before halting. Project-wide deficiencies that belong to later, not-yet-dispatched stories must not halt the current story.

correction: STORY-02-004 (Liquibase DDL) was routed to ingestion by the registry, but update-ingestion refused (out of its domain), and update-scaffold also routed out citing the same registry mapping. Both skills disclaim ownership of ddl/liquibase/**.
pattern: When a story routes to a skill that immediately ROUTE-OUTs based on its hard rules, the registry has a gap. Either (a) extend a skill to own that path class explicitly, or (b) add a new specialized skill (e.g. create-liquibase). Until then, orchestrator should detect double-route-out and either fall back to direct edits or block the batch with a clear error rather than thrashing between skills.

correction: TaskGroup factory pattern using dag=None + TaskGroup-context fallback breaks under Airflow 3.x @dag decorators; TaskGroup eagerly validates dag is truthy.
pattern: In Airflow 3.x, resolve the active DAG via airflow.sdk.definitions._internal.contextmanager.DagContext.get_current() and pass explicitly to factories rather than relying on contextual binding.

correction: STORY-02-008 (local integration test of Bronze DAG against Unity Catalog) and STORY-02-009 (deploy validation: Liquibase apply + DAG smoke) had no owning create-/update- skill. All four candidate skills (update-ingestion/dag/scaffold/pipeline) ROUTE-OUT.
pattern: Stories whose deliverables live under tests/integration/, docs/runbooks/, or deploy-validation scripts have no current owning skill. Either: (a) add an integration-test domain to update-ingestion or update-dag, (b) introduce a dedicated create-integration-test / create-runbook skill, or (c) flag such stories as manual at backlog-generation time so implement-stories does not attempt to dispatch them.

correction: STORY-02-004 handbook validator returned 29 pre-existing CRITICAL findings (duplicate synthea_* configs vs LLD §5.1 short-name configs, missing output_path, missing tests, absolute /opt/airflow path) that are entirely outside this story scope (which only touched ddl/liquibase/changelogs/*.xml + master-changelog.xml). The Step 3.4 gate as written halts story progression on whole-project violations even when the story scope is fully passing.
pattern: Step 3.4 handbook validator should distinguish story-scope failures from project-wide pre-existing failures. Consider scoping the validator to the dispatched .skill-paths set, or whitelist pre-existing findings via a baseline file, so a story does not get halted by failures unrelated to its deliverables.

correction: Newly added skill folders create-integration-test/ and create-deploy-validation/ exist on disk under developer-plugin/skills/ but the Skill tool refuses to invoke them with Unknown skill: developer-plugin:create-integration-test. Apparently new skills require a plugin reinstall or marketplace refresh before they become invokable in the running session.
pattern: When adding new skill folders to a plugin mid-session, document the reload step (e.g. /plugin reload or marketplace refresh) in the create-role-plugin / skill-scaffolding handbook. implement-stories should surface this with a clear actionable error rather than silently failing dispatch when a fallback_kind resolves to an existing-but-unregistered skill.

correction: Wired spark_catalog to UCSingleCatalog; saveAsTable fails because v2 catalog routes through Spark v1 SessionCatalog. spark-expectations always calls saveAsTable so the whole pipeline blocks.
pattern: For local-FS dev stacks DO NOT wire spark_catalog to UCSingleCatalog. Use DeltaCatalog (org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog) + Spark's built-in Hive metastore. UC server may run for UI/lineage but not as the Spark catalog.

correction: Each spark-submit boots a fresh in-memory catalog by default, losing table registrations. Next task sees Delta files but no metastore entry and fails DELTA_CREATE_TABLE_WITH_NON_EMPTY_LOCATION.
pattern: Set spark.sql.catalogImplementation=hive AND spark.hadoop.javax.jdo.option.ConnectionURL='jdbc:derby:;databaseName=<stable-path>;create=true' so Derby state persists across task runs.

correction: Used DuckDB Python connector + to_pylist for source reads; observations/procedures OOM at 1g driver memory.
pattern: Default per-table YAML source.type=csv (let Spark read natively). Reserve duckdb source type for tables <100MB. Document the OOM risk.

correction: Tried to pass driver_cores= to Airflow 3.x SparkSubmitOperator; TypeError at DAG parse.
pattern: Airflow 3.x SparkSubmitOperator dropped the driver_cores kwarg. Forward the value via spark.driver.cores in the conf dict.

correction: Wrote se.run_dq as decorated = se.with_expectations(...)(df). with_expectations returns a decorator expecting a fn that returns DF, so 'validated' was a function and df.write failed.
pattern: Always wrap the input df in a no-arg lambda: decorated = se.with_expectations(...)(lambda: df); validated = decorated().

correction: Tried to set se.enable.stats.table=False to bypass UC catalog issues; key does not exist, stats writes still happened.
pattern: spark-expectations always writes a stats table — there is no disable flag. Design the metastore to accept saveAsTable from SE (Hive/Derby works; UCSingleCatalog does not).

correction: Relied on spark-submit CWD for resolving relative paths in per-table YAML (contracts_dir, dq_rules_dir, source.database, source.path). CWD inside Airflow worker is /opt/airflow, not the project root.
pattern: Add a PATIENT360_PROJECT_ROOT env var and an _anchor_relative helper in the runner that joins relative YAML paths against it. docker-compose env block must export this var to /opt/patient_360 (or whatever the in-container project root is).

correction: Generated DAG with max_active_tasks=16 and catchup=True. Concurrent tasks raced on shared bronze_se_stats CREATE; backfill avalanche piled up scheduled runs and orphan Delta files.
pattern: Dev DAG defaults: max_active_tasks=1 and catchup=False. Document that production raises these only after the SE stats table has been seeded by at least one successful run.

correction: DEV compute defaults were 2g driver / 2g executor; with Spark + Airflow + UC + Postgres all in an 8GB Docker cap the driver got SIGKILL'd (exit -9) leaving orphan Delta files.
pattern: Default DEV memory: 1g driver / 1g executor / shuffle_partitions=4 / broadcast=10m. Document the trade-off (large tables like observations may need raises).

correction: Reconciliation_bronze was generated as a PythonOperator running PySpark in-process. Airflow 3.x task-SDK collides with py4j subprocess management: _start_update_server() missing 1 required positional argument: 'is_unix_domain_sock'.
pattern: Any task that touches Spark must use SparkSubmitOperator (own JVM). PythonOperator with build_spark_session inside the callable is forbidden under Airflow 3.x.

correction: Reconciliation queried 3-part FQN unity.bronze.bronze_se_stats; with UC dropped this is REQUIRES_SINGLE_PART_NAMESPACE.
pattern: Use 2-part FQNs (schema.table) throughout when spark_catalog is the default catalog. The catalog name (unity/spark_catalog) never appears in writer or query code; it is only relevant for catalog config.

correction: Reconciliation tried to match on Airflow ts_nodash as meta_dq_run_id; spark-expectations generates its own run_id internally and does not accept an external override.
pattern: SE evidence check filters on meta_dq_run_date (= Airflow ds) only — NOT on meta_dq_run_id. The contract proves 'DQ ran for today's data', not 'DQ ran for this exact Airflow run'.

correction: STORY-03-001 (Silver SCD2 dimension) classified as 'ingestion' (slug match /silver/ -> ingestion); create-ingestion ROUTE-OUT to create-silver, which does not exist as a registered skill in developer-plugin.
pattern: When the content classifier maps a silver/* (or any non-Bronze layer) story to 'ingestion' purely via an epic-slug substring match, and the dispatched create-ingestion ROUTE-OUTs to a create-silver/create-gold skill that is NOT registered in the plugin, HALT the batch with an actionable error (missing owner skill). Do not re-dispatch into the route-out target (no thrash). Fix path: either add the create-silver/create-gold skills, or correct the classifier so silver/gold stories do not resolve to 'ingestion'. (L-008, L-011)

correction: Dispatched create-silver via Skill tool with args=STORY-03-001 and wrote .skill-arg/.skill-paths, but the forked sub-skill received neither $ARGUMENTS nor consumed the scoping files; it ran FULL mode (13 tables) instead of story scope, and left .skill-arg/.skill-paths on disk.
pattern: When a forked create-/update- skill leaves .skill-arg/.skill-paths un-consumed after dispatch, treat it as a scope-control failure: the sub-skill did not honor story scoping. Surface a CRITICAL (do not silently accept full-mode output) and confirm scope with the user before continuing the batch. Fix the sub-skills to read .skill-arg as the authoritative target when $ARGUMENTS is empty in fork context.

correction: DMS §3 and STM Bronze-to-Silver disagree on ~14 Silver column names/types/PK columns (e.g. patients calculated_age/patient_status vs patient_age/is_deceased; name_prefix vs prefix; synthetic *_id SHA-256 PK columns present in STM but absent in DMS §3; billing_claims diagnosis_code_3/referring_provider_id present in DMS but absent in STM). The skill mandates 'never invent columns; every output column from DMS §3' AND 'preserve STM transform expressions' — these are mutually unsatisfiable when DMS and STM diverge.
pattern: Before generating Silver modules, run a DMS§3-vs-STM column reconciliation gate. If they diverge on column name/type/PK/presence for any table, HALT and route to data-modeler:update-dms or mapping-analyst:update-stm rather than silently picking one artifact. Do not invent a merged schema.

correction: Default story arg STORY-03-001 AC text references 'unity.bronze.synthea_patients' (UC 3-part FQN, UC-managed) but LLD §13 Decisions 12+15 are Revoked (2026-05-12) and LLD-DEVIATIONS.md mandates path-based external Delta read via read_bronze_delta 2-part FQN (IL-002/IL-004). The story AC is stale vs the re-approved LLD.
pattern: When a story AC's path/FQN convention conflicts with a Revoked LLD decision that LLD-DEVIATIONS.md has already superseded, follow the LLD+deviations (authoritative) and recommend scrum-master:update-stories to refresh the stale AC text — per IL-017 do not rename project code to match the stale AC.

correction: se_runner.run_dq returns a single validated DataFrame (keyword-only args: df, *, table, env, dq_rules_dir, action_if_failed, quarantine_path) and resolves rules via dq_rules/{table}.yml|.yaml. The create-silver SKILL Phase 3 sketch shows 'validated_df, _quarantine = run_dq(df=..., action_if_failed=...)' (tuple return, positional df) which does not match the shipped API.
pattern: Generate Silver transform calls against the SHIPPED se_runner.run_dq signature (single-DF return, keyword-only) not the SKILL sketch. Also: DQS emits se-rules-<dashed>.yaml; these must be copied to dq_rules/{table}.yml (underscored, no se-rules- prefix) for run_dq's convention-based discovery.

correction: verify_acs.py pytest check ran bare 'python3 -m pytest' and reported AC5 FAIL (exit=2 import error) though tests pass 11/11 via 'uv run --extra dev' in the project venv
pattern: verify_acs.py pytest checks must run via 'uv run' from the project root (like validate_silver.py) so the editable package + dev extras resolve; a bare interpreter yields false-negative AC FAILs that orchestrator must not treat as halts

correction: create-silver did not consume the .skill-arg/.skill-paths scoping files after a story-mode run (it routed correctly but left both files on disk)
pattern: per L-001, when scoping files survive a sub-skill invocation but the deliverables match the story scope, treat it as a sub-skill consumption bug (not a routing failure): clean up the files and note it; fix create-/update- skills to delete .skill-arg/.skill-paths after reading

correction: STORY-03-002 AC1 cites unity.bronze.synthea_organizations (UC-managed; LLD Decision 15), but LLD Decisions 12&15 were revoked 2026-05-12 making the bronze read path-based. The implementation is correct per current LLD; the AC verification grep string is stale.
pattern: When an AC Verification grep targets a literal that a later-revoked LLD decision invalidated (e.g. a UC FQN replaced by a path-based read), the AC spec is stale, not the code. Do not patch code to satisfy a stale grep; surface to scrum-master:update-stories to re-sync AC text against the current LLD decision log, and treat the inline-FAIL as a backlog spec defect rather than an implementation defect.

summary: STM v3 Bronze-to-Silver mandates CAST(REVENUE AS DECIMAL(14,2)) but DMS §3.11 still reads DECIMAL(12,2). Resolved in favor of STM (authoritative for transformation logic per update-silver diff rules). Recommend an update-dms cycle to reconcile DMS §3.11 revenue type to DECIMAL(14,2). Also DMS §3.11 state=VARCHAR(2) vs STM v3 state=VARCHAR(50) — string column, no code impact, contract follows DMS string typing.

correction: STORY-03-007 AC1 Verification used literal grep for task ids transform_patients_silver/transform_payers_silver, but the DAG generates them via f"transform_{table}_silver" loop, so the literal strings are absent though the task ids exist at parse time (proven by AC4/AC5 pytest PASS).
pattern: When an AC Verification grep targets a string that the implementation produces dynamically (f-string / loop-generated task ids, config-driven names), a literal grep yields a false FAIL. Treat as a Verification-spec defect (L-004 sibling): recommend scrum-master:update-stories to replace the literal grep with the runtime pytest assertion (which already validates the generated ids), rather than forcing the generator to hardcode strings. Do not rewrite working code to satisfy a brittle grep.

correction: Pinned pyspark 4.1.2 alongside delta-spark 4.3.0; uv sync failed because delta-spark 4.3.0 declares requires_dist pyspark<=4.1.1,>=4.0.1.

On the Spark 4.1 line, delta-spark 4.2.0/4.3.0 cap pyspark<=4.1.1 — pin pyspark 4.1.1, NOT 4.1.2. pyspark, the Spark JVM (Docker base), delta-spark, and the UC connector unitycatalog-spark_4.1_2.13 must all stay lockstep on the same Spark major.minor.

pattern: se_runner's bare-name target fallback defaults to the BRONZE schema (unity.bronze.<table>). Silver/Gold dq_rules dq_env.<ENV>.table_name MUST be the explicit 3-part FQN unity.<schema>.<table> — a bare name routes the managed SE _error/_stats audit tables into the bronze schema AND, because SE filters rules on table_name == target_table, matches ZERO rules (silently disabling DQ).

correction: Set DQ_REC reconciliation rules is_active:true to 'enforce' the critical-table fail-action; the bronze tasks then failed with PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR in source_query_dq.
pattern: SE inline reconciliation rules (rule_type query_dq, tag reconciliation, DQ_REC_*) MUST stay is_active:false on this stack. Their expectation references the DuckDB SOURCE table (e.g. synthea.<t>) which se_runner does NOT register as a Spark view at SE-run time (it only registers unity.* + bare-name views), and the CASE...FROM...@-delimiter form does not parse as an SE query_dq. Activating one raises SparkExpectationsMiscException: PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR at FROM and fails the task. Keep the rule PRESENT with action_if_failed:fail (satisfies test_ac3_critical_tables_have_fail_action) but is_active:false (matches every shipped DQ_REC_*). Cross-table reconciliation is done by the reconciliation_bronze/silver TASK (utils/reconciliation.py), not by inline SE query_dq.

correction: reconciliation_bronze SE-RUN-EVIDENCE gate failed for a backfill (dags test of a past logical date): it queries the managed SE stats with WHERE meta_dq_run_date = '{ds}', but meta_dq_run_date is the SE WALL-CLOCK run date, not the data ds. Running ds=2026-06-20 today (2026-06-21) -> 0 matching rows -> false 'SE never ran' failure.
pattern: The SE-RUN-EVIDENCE gate in bronze/reconciliation.py (_count_se_stats_rows / assert_se_evidence) must NOT assume the SE stats meta_dq_run_date equals the data ds. The managed SE _stats table has no ds column; meta_dq_run_date/meta_dq_run_datetime are the wall-clock SE run time. The `WHERE meta_dq_run_date = '{ds}'` filter only works when the run happens on the same calendar day as ds (normal scheduled hourly run) and FALSE-FAILS on any backfill/replay of a past ds. Fix: either filter by meta_dq_run_date = current_date() (SE ran in this execution), or thread the DAG's meta_dq_run_id into se_runner so SE stamps the stats and the gate matches on meta_dq_run_id exactly. Do not gate anti-silent-skip on ds == run-date.
